posts.content_md: could you suggest me some good books or web pages on basic and holograpy ,or if you have a book could you send it to me: [istar@hi.t-com.hr](mailto:istar@hi.t-com.hr)

posts.author: Tony
posts.content_md:
for basic web links see:

[http://www.3dimagery.com/index.html](http://www.3dimagery.com/index.html)

[http://members.aol.com/gakall/holopg.html](http://members.aol.com/gakall/holopg.html)

[http://www.holoworld.com/](http://www.holoworld.com/)

[http://www.disp.duke.edu/~dbrady/ece371 ... /holo.html](http://www.disp.duke.edu/~dbrady/ece371/labs/lab8/holo.html)

[http://www.fou.uib.no/fd/1996/h/404001/kap02.htm](http://www.fou.uib.no/fd/1996/h/404001/kap02.htm)

...and for a more rigorous explanation with some math, see:

[http://splweb.bwh.harvard.edu:8000/cour ... index.html](http://splweb.bwh.harvard.edu:8000/courses/mas450/reading/chaptersPDF/index.html)

for books, see 'Holography Handbook' by Unterseher et al,

or any edition of Saxby's 'Practical Holography' (rare, expensive).
